about.title: Maywood Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Maywood is a small, tightly packed city, and even one traffic death ripples through the whole community. Public crash records show 63 injury collisions and 79 injured people in the most recent year, with fatal outcomes far less common but devastating when they happen — often on higher-volume streets like Atlantic Boulevard, Pine Avenue, or 59th Place, and frequently during Friday evening rush hours. If your family has lost a loved one in a crash, California law allows certain surviving family members to pursue a wrongful death claim to recover specific losses. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free connection service that puts grieving families in touch with an independent personal injury attorney in the network who can review what happened and explain the options, without any pressure or upfront cost. You focus on your family — we help you find someone to talk to about the legal side.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Maywood Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to certain people — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents or heirs. We help connect you with an attorney who can explain whether your family qualifies to bring a claim.

items.title: We Know the Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Connecting early with an attorney helps make sure that window doesn't close.

items.title: We Focus on What Can Actually Be Recovered
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California can address funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — losses that are real but not always obvious. An attorney in our network can walk your family through what may apply to your situation.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can look at your family's specific situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensating the family, even if criminal charges are filed, dropped, or never pursued at all. The two processes run independently of each other.

items.question: Was the crash on a street like Atlantic Boulevard or Pine Avenue relevant to our case?
items.answer: Details like which Maywood corridor a fatal crash happened on, and what time it occurred, can matter for gathering evidence such as traffic signals, witness accounts, or nearby camera footage. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help figure out what records might be available for your specific situation.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family recovers compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
